technicalPrinciples.title: How JPEG Compression Works
technicalPrinciples.description: Understanding the technical principles behind JPEG compression helps you make informed decisions about your images.

items.title: Lossy Compression Algorithm
items.description: JPEG uses a sophisticated lossy compression algorithm that strategically removes imperceptible visual details to achieve high compression ratios. The algorithm analyzes the image and discards information that the human eye cannot easily detect, balancing file size with visual quality.
benefits: Ideal for photographs and complex images

items.title: DCT (Discrete Cosine Transform)
items.description: JPEG compression employs the Discrete Cosine Transform to convert image data from the spatial domain to the frequency domain. This mathematical transformation allows the algorithm to identify and compress redundant information more efficiently, particularly in areas with subtle color variations.

items.title: Quantization and Quality Control
items.description: After DCT transformation, quantization is applied to reduce the precision of less important frequency components. The quality setting (1-100%) directly controls this quantization process, allowing users to fine-tune the balance between compression ratio and visual fidelity.

items.title: Chroma Subsampling
items.description: JPEG takes advantage of the human eye's lower sensitivity to color information compared to brightness. Chroma subsampling reduces color resolution while maintaining full luminance detail, achieving additional compression without noticeable quality loss in most images.

bestPractices.title: JPEG Compression Best Practices
bestPractices.description: Follow these expert tips to get the best results from JPEG compression.

tips.title: Master Quality-Size Trade-off
tips.content: Quality 85 is the sweet spot for web photos—nearly identical to original but 50-70% smaller. Use 90-95 for professional photography portfolios, 80-85 for social media, and 60-75 for thumbnails or previews. Avoid recompressing JPEG files to prevent generational quality loss.

tips.title: Optimize Chroma Subsampling
tips.content: Use 4:2:0 chroma subsampling for maximum compression (standard for web). Use 4:2:2 for images with text or fine color details, and 4:4:4 only for professional printing. Proper subsampling can reduce file size by 30% without noticeable quality loss in photographs.

tips.title: Know JPEG's Strengths & Limits
tips.content: JPEG excels at photographs, natural scenes, and images with gradients. Avoid JPEG for screenshots, text, logos, or line art—these show visible compression artifacts. Never use JPEG for images requiring transparency. For modern web apps, consider WebP as a JPEG alternative with 25-35% better compression.

tips.title: Smart Batch Compression Strategy
tips.content: Group photos by use case: use progressive JPEG for images over 50KB (better perceived loading), baseline for smaller images. Apply higher quality (90+) to hero images and portraits, moderate quality (80-85) to content images, and lower quality (60-75) to background images or thumbnails.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.description: Common questions about JPEG compression and our JPEG compressor tool.

items.question: What is JPEG compression and how does it work?
items.answer: JPEG compression is a lossy compression method that reduces file size by removing visually imperceptible details. It uses Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) and quantization to achieve 50-90% file size reduction while maintaining good visual quality for photographs.

items.question: What quality setting should I use for JPEG compression?
items.answer: For web images, use 80-90% quality for optimal balance. For print materials, use 90-95%. For thumbnails or previews, 60-80% is sufficient. Higher quality means larger files but better visual fidelity.

items.question: Is JPEG compression lossless or lossy?
items.answer: Standard JPEG uses lossy compression, meaning some image data is permanently discarded to reduce file size. While lossless JPEG variants exist, they're rarely used because they don't provide significant compression benefits over PNG.

items.question: When should I use JPEG instead of PNG?
items.answer: Use JPEG for photographs, realistic images, and complex scenes with many colors. Use PNG for graphics, logos, screenshots, and images requiring transparency or perfect pixel-level accuracy. JPEG typically provides 10x better compression for photos.

items.question: What is progressive JPEG and should I use it?
items.answer: Progressive JPEG loads images in multiple passes, showing a low-resolution version first that gradually improves. This provides better perceived loading speed on slower connections and is recommended for web images larger than 10KB.

items.question: Does JPEG support transparency?
items.answer: No, JPEG doesn't support transparency or alpha channels. If you need transparency, use PNG for lossless or WebP for lossy compression with transparency support.

items.question: How much can I compress a JPEG without losing quality?
items.answer: You can typically compress JPEG by 50-70% with minimal visible quality loss using 85-90% quality settings. Beyond that, artifacts may become noticeable depending on the image content and viewing conditions.

items.question: Will compressing an already compressed JPEG reduce quality further?
items.answer: Yes, each time you compress an already-compressed JPEG, you introduce additional quality loss (generation loss). Always work from the original uncompressed image when possible to maintain best quality.

items.question: Can I batch compress multiple JPEG files?
items.answer: Yes, our tool supports batch processing of multiple JPEG files simultaneously. You can compress up to 10 files at once with consistent quality settings, saving time while maintaining uniform results.

items.question: Is my data safe when using this online compressor?
items.answer: Absolutely! All compression happens locally in your browser using JavaScript. Your images never leave your device or get uploaded to our servers, ensuring complete privacy and security.
